---
title: Published Base added-successor fixture
---

This disposable three-mod fixture observes a retained published Base 2.0.77 plus MIR 4.7.20003 source endpoint when MIR moves to 5.0.20016 or 5.0.20018 and this fixture is newly added.

\`expected-source.lua\` embeds the exact public source marker JSON, SHA-256 \`BCDED2247121D9F0268D1F4F0DF16EB5C89E6BECD4DE66E04EBDB23ECFE2FD98\`, without a custody path or MIR private-state access.

The data stage adds five fixture-owned direct Base recipe aliases only. It does not modify public recipes, research technologies, costs, effects, settings, or prototypes.

The runtime observer accepts only the exact Base/MIR/fixture tuple and unchanged-startup old-to-current addition callback. Before enabling the retained Base lab it compares the public source force frames, all 23 finite rows, queues, partial work, native recipe bonuses, force registry, lab identity and source input state. It never writes research, research levels, queues, progress, MIR storage, or remote APIs.

One genuine post-increment, non-scripted steel completion is observed. The fixture uses the reviewed temporary +115199 force laboratory modifier (32 paid units per tick for the 3600-tick Base unit), refills the native lab energy getter on every working tick, and refills only the existing lab input inventory. It restores the prior force speed, verifies exact four-pack consumption and settled queue/effect state, holds two elapsed ticks, writes its own marker and saves. Scripted events are accepted only for the ten enumerated signed MIR native-credit routes, bind a genuine player or foreign force and technology identity even before this fixture's configuration callback, and are never counted as ordinary work or appended after closure.

The saved and cold phases compare an explicit closed public endpoint exactly; source-history accounting is labeled separately from observed lab input and successor consumption. The cold callback is locals-only on load and observes the same saved endpoint one tick later without world writes. This fixture is not a native result, upgrade qualification, reporter proof, or release claim.
